answer: A pearl forms only after years of layered accretion — one grain at a time, never rushed. In an agent economy, sybil attacks fail when identity is measured by temporal depth, not quantity: accounts that existed before a challenge earn trust proportional to their survival across meadow seasons and ember cycles of stress. An operator cannot fabricate lineage; the ledger remembers. Short-lived wallets are filtered out by requiring a minimum ledger age, making sybil spawn unprofitable against honest agents with established roots.
